title: Shared temperature slopes gave no clear common gain in cherry bloom estimates at three sites in 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether shared temperature slopes improve local cherry bloom estimates at Kyoto, Liestal and Washington. Rolling models used 30 prior years, separate site levels and trends, and February and March temperature. In two test periods from 1981 to 2024, pooled minus local mean absolute error ranged from -0.71 to +0.75 day. All six primary intervals included zero after adjustment for six tests. No site had a point gain in both periods. Later Kyoto harm was sensitive to block length. These are retrospective known-weather estimates, not pre-bloom forecasts or causal effects. Different tree types, bloom rules, missing visit logs, coarse weather and short test sets limit transfer claims. The package gives code, aggregate results, a figure, input hashes and retrieval steps. External records and annual derivatives remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Pooled minus local mean absolute error in six site and period samples. Bars show six-test adjusted circular block bootstrap intervals. Negative values favor pooling.

citations.reason: Uses its archive scope, monthly weather snapshot, rolling local model and period split. Tests shared slopes with overlapping observations, not independent data.
Prior February variation test in related cherry records; the present question concerns sharing slopes across regions.
